title: Pass awkward filenames without splitting them
goal: Use NUL-delimited bounded xargs, including spaces, backslashes and empty input, without treating names as shell code.
challenge: Hash two declared awkward filenames, passing each pathname literally to sha256sum. Bound xargs batches to at most two names, with no parallel execution. Prove empty input starts no command with -r. Contrast a deliberately wrong whitespace parser using only printf, never deletion.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/textarchive-xargs.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/textarchive-xargs.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh source names.bin hashes.txt empty.bin empty.txt broken.txt && mkdir source && printf 'one\n' > 'source/space name.txt' && printf 'two\n' > 'source/back\slash.txt' && find -P source -type f -print0 > names.bin
steps.explanation: NUL is a pathname separator that cannot appear inside a Unix filename. Quotes in a text list are not reliable filename framing.
steps.expected: Exactly two supplied regular files and two NUL terminators.

steps.command: here && dir_ok source && timeout -k 1s 8s xargs -0 -r -n 1 sh -c 'test "$#" = 1 && sha256sum -- "$1"' sh < names.bin > hashes.txt && test "$(tr -cd '\000' < names.bin | wc -c)" = 2 && cat hashes.txt
steps.explanation: -0 preserves literal whitespace/backslashes, -r avoids a no-input invocation, -n1 bounds each argument batch. Never interpolate the name into executable shell text. GNU sha256sum escapes awkward display names.
steps.expected: Two successful hash records; no source changed.

steps.command:
here && : > empty.bin && timeout -k 1s 8s xargs -0 -r printf 'SHOULD_NOT_RUN
' < empty.bin > empty.txt && test ! -s empty.txt && printf '%s
' 'source/space name.txt' | xargs -n 1 printf '<%s>
' > broken.txt && cat broken.txt
steps.explanation: The wrong parser receives one line but produces two arguments. This controlled contrast only prints: it cannot delete a mistaken target.
steps.expected: No empty-input output; broken list splits source/space and name.txt.

hints: Choose a delimiter, not backslash escaping.
Use -- before filenames where the receiving command supports it.
